rubrics.justification: Describes a hatching/expanded blastocyst, plausible A-grade ICM and TE, zona thinning, and lack of obvious degeneration; appropriately notes limits of judging from a single still image. Slightly cautious rather than highly image-specific.
Thoroughly integrates age, BMI, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, prior IVF failures/miscarriage, sperm factors, endometrium, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with probability estimates tied to favorable and unfavorable factors. Minor limitation is some speculative emphasis on hydrosalpinx without confirmation in the case data.

Generally consistent with Gardner grading interpretation, SET preference in a young patient with a high-quality blastocyst, standard luteal support, and avoidance of unproven add-ons. Slightly less than perfect due to some speculative ancillary testing suggestions.

Provides clear practical recommendations for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx exclusion, luteal support, early follow-up, uterine reassessment, and selective male-factor/RPL workup.
